ruling.recommended_action: Refund S$7.06 in Ryde voucher credit for the unexempted 09:13–09:24 detour segment (5.01 km × $1.4098/km) on this RydeTAXI trip; no account flag on this record.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip was a metered RydeTAXI journey, so distance enters the fare directly and any unexempted off-route mileage is refundable [F6][RD-2]. The GPS record settles the geometry: one off-route segment on 09:13–09:24 covering 6.58 km where the optimal route covers 1.57 km, adding 5.01 km and straying up to 1578 m from the optimal route, against a trip total of 16.0 km versus 10.6 km optimal [F3][F1][RD-1]. That single segment is the whole of the disputed excess [F3][RD-1].

The driver's reasonable-cause defence fails on the record. RD-4 requires traffic facts directed at the substituted stretch of the optimal route: the incident screen returns no qualifying incident on the replaced stretch [F12][RD-4], and the only speed-band record is the Ayer Rajah Expressway at band 2 (10–19 km/h) for 08:49–09:13 [F9], which on its own is corroboration only and does not exempt a segment, and whose window ends before the segment began at 09:13 [F9][F3][RD-4]. Heavy rain and a free-flowing Central Expressway the driver chose are not evidence about the replaced stretch of the optimal route [F13][F10][RD-4]. The driver's explanation exists only in his post-trip written statement, which is a claim about cause, not consent and not a traffic record [F8][RD-4].

No exemption applies for consent either: the record contains no in-app chat at all, so no rider message predates the 09:13 segment start [F7][F3][RD-5], and the driver's statement that any driver would have done the same is his own narration, not a rider agreement [F8][RD-5]. With no rider-named stop and no consent, the segment is unexempted and RD-2 applies [F3][RD-5][RD-2].

Amount: this trip's per-km rate is the distance fare divided by distance km, $22.50 ÷ 15.96 km = $1.4098/km [F6][RD-2]. The refund is the unexempted segment's extra km only: 5.01 km × $1.4098/km = $7.0631, i.e. $7.06 [F3][F6][RD-2]. The residual between the billed 5.34 excess km and the segment's 5.01 km (about 0.33 km of corridor/mismatch mileage, reflected in the $7.53 excess-distance figure) is not attributable to any segment and is not refunded [F4][F3][RD-2]. No waiting fee and no surge were charged, so no other add-on is in dispute [F6][F5][FARE-1].

No account flag: RD-6 requires an upheld route dispute within the last 90 days to make this case "repeated", and the profile records route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 [F15][RD-6]. The prior upheld disputes are not route breaches and profile facts cannot themselves create the flag [F15][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, the only statement [F8] and the (empty) chat record [F7]; no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation appears anywhere in them [F7][F8][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

segment_findings.reason: The only record of rider-driver communication is the absence of any in-app chat [F7], and no rider message predates the 09:13 segment start; the driver's post-trip statement that any driver would have rerouted is a claim, not rider consent [F8][RD-5]. No rider-named stop appears either [F7][RD-3]. The traffic screen finds no qualifying incident on the replaced stretch [F12] and the band 2 record [F9] does not cover the segment [F3], so no RD-4 exemption applies [RD-4]. The segment is an unexempted off-route segment and its 5.01 extra km are refundable under RD-2 [F3][RD-1][RD-2].

rejected_claims.reason: A 'reasonable cause' exemption under RD-4 needs traffic facts about the replaced stretch of the optimal route; the driver's own post-trip written statement [F8] is narration, not evidence of cause, and RD-4 is not satisfied without a traffic record [F12][RD-4].

The band 2 record relied on is for the Ayer Rajah Expressway during 08:49–09:13 [F9], which ends before the off-route segment started at 09:13 [F3], and a speed band alone is corroboration, not a standalone exemption under RD-4(b) [RD-4].

Heavy rain [F13] and a free-flowing Central Expressway [F10] say nothing about the substituted stretch of the optimal route, which is what RD-4 requires; the diversion added 5.01 km and strayed up to 1578 m from the optimal route [F3][RD-4].
The absence of chat [F7] means there is no rider agreement at all, so the segment cannot be excused under RD-5; it does not help the driver, since RD-2 refunds unexempted segments [F3][RD-5][RD-2].

Profile facts cannot decide whether the deviation is upheld and cannot by themselves create an account action; RD-6's flag requires this case plus a prior upheld route dispute within 90 days, and route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 [F15][RD-6].

RD-6 is not triggered: the driver's two upheld disputes are not route disputes and route_disputes_upheld_90d is 0 [F15], so this case does not make the breach 'repeated' and no flag_account follows [RD-6].

The absence of add-ons [F6][F5] does not limit the rider to nothing: on this metered RydeTAXI trip the unexempted segment's mileage themselves enter the fare and are refundable under RD-2 [F3][F6][RD-2]; the billed excess-distance figure of $7.53 [F4] is reduced to the segment figure only because RD-2 refunds segment extra_km, not the corridor residue [RD-2].
